chunks: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Dirraj from ash-Sha'iri from Al-Hakam ibn Utaibah said:

We were at the door of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). A woman came and asked, 'Which of you is Abu Ja'far?' She was told, 'What do you want from him?' She said, 'I want to ask him a question.' They said to her, 'This is the jurist of the people of Iraq, so ask him.' She said, 'My husband died and left one thousand dirhams. I have a dowry of five hundred dirhams due from him. I took my dowry and took my inheritance from what remained. Then a man came and claimed one thousand dirhams from him, and I testified to that against my husband.' Al-Hakam said, 'While we were calculating what she would receive, Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) came out. We informed him of the woman's statement and what she had asked about. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, "She acknowledged to him one-third of what is in her hand, and she has no inheritance."' Al-Hakam said, 'By Allah, I have not seen anyone more understanding than Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The relied-upon ruling is that when a person acknowledges a debt to an heir, it binds him from her to the extent of what she receives in her share, and the entire debt does not bind him. As for the narration of Isma'il ibn 'Ammar, in which he said 'it binds him that in her share,' its apparent meaning does not indicate that the entire debt binds him. It is possible he meant 'he binds him from that in her share to the extent of what she receives,' interpreting it to mean that is understood from the context of the situation or from the explanation that preceded from them. And we have cited what indicates that, which is the narration of Abu al-Bakhtari and Al-Hakam ibn Utaibah, and the narration of Mansur ibn Hazim regarding acknowledgment of manumission, which also testifies to that. And on this basis, there is no contradiction between the reports.

key_terms.إِقْرَار: Acknowledgment or confession of a debt or right

ai.seo_question: How is a debt acknowledged by the deceased handled in Islamic inheritance law?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of al-Shaykh al-Tusi, illustrates Imam al-Sadiq’s precise legal reasoning regarding 'iqrar' (acknowledgment) of debt by the deceased, establishing that the debt is satisfied solely from the acknowledging heir's portion rather than the entire estate. The text further resolves apparent contradictions in other narrations by interpreting them contextually, a methodological nuance highlighted by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Shaykh al-Mufid to ensure consistency within Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the principle that an heir’s acknowledgment binds only their specific share, preserving the rights of other heirs from being diminished by a single heir's admission.
